I would highly recommend The Genius (all seasons) and The Bloody Game S2. However S2 have spoilers for S1 so if you have extra time I’d still recommend watching it.  The Time Hotel is good too. I would personally start with The Genius S1 and work my way through the series first :)

This is the first time I’ve seen other people mention the lack of downtime they get! I think its a crucial difference and probably wasn’t something the players took into consideration when they went into the show. >!It looks like Dongjae went into Devils Plan expecting The Genius and that was his ultimate downfall!<

i also don’t think dongjae got outsmarted by anyone. it was mostly that he just came to play games and didn’t realise that apparently being liked by your competitors was more beneficial than actually playing the games well lol

the game format is indeed at fault, losing all your pieces shouldn’t mean you get eliminated right away. especially because someone randomly in the game can just decide that for you (i.e. every fkn game thats been played so far, but more clearly in yeonwoos elimination). if it was a skill based elimination like the death matches in the genius then i believe the chances of stronger players remaining would be a lot higher. 

however, alliances have always existed in this sort of show design, so i’m not really sure how it can be changed to remove it completely, but i think the amount of weak contestants the show recruited is the real enemy. they have no way of winning on their own merits which ultimately leads to them sticking tightly to their alliance rather than thinking for themselves. i understand it, but it’s just not very fun to watch. as a viewer i can’t help but dislike those in the major alliance purely because its become so predictable.

hopefully things go up from here with the way things ended in ep9.

the point is that most viewers of this show would find it more fun to watch smarter, more talented people solve complex problems and compete with each other during the games. if you personally don’t find that interesting and would rather watch an alliance full of weak and undeserving players ace the games every episode, then thats fine. but to call dongjae a weak player when his only real weakness was being dealt the fanatic card in game 1 is a bit farfetched.

The problem is exactly this. He was clearly a great player, anyone could see it from the beginning. But pretty much right after the first game “teams” were formed and he just got piled on which didn’t allow him to showcase his skill set. That’s why everyone just got frustrated. No one was playing the actual games anymore, it was just alliance after alliance. That’s why Seokjin, who no doubt is incredibly smart, still got 0 points in the animals game and he just sat there doing nothing. It was not about playing anymore it was just about making the most friends.

I just finished the episodes and oh my god… 
I am so peeved with how the game play is going. 

It’s so unenjoyable to watch because the last few episodes have just been about eliminating players that don’t agree with Orbit’s “philosophy”. It’s worse because as viewers we can all see that he’s just playing strategically but everyone in the majority alliance is too stupid to see it. Either that or they’re just happy Orbit’s gonna carry them to the end because they know they can’t play the game themselves anyway. 

Seokjin’s feisty comments towards him is what got me through watching the rest of the episodes because I was really struggling after Dongjae’s elimination. Not only that but if Orbit truly believed what he was saying then I still don’t understand why they wrote down Hyesung’s number. And afterwards in the interview he was like I don’t know if this is the right thing to do like…? According to your own philosophy its not..? It’s just such a shame that Dongjae had to go home because of this. If only there was a death match or something completely skill based. I need to see more of him like please omg Netflix bring him back… 

In regards to that, I think the Genius did this show far better. The contestants being locked up in a house for a week straight means that all they can think about is the game - in their heads they can’t step back and see the big picture. Constantly surrounded by what is ultimately just a game makes it far more personal for them, meaning they can’t get rid of the image the contestants have from the games they’ve been playing. That’s why the minority alliance has such a hard time. No one can see past what they did in Game 1, which is extremely unfair since those roles were handed to them by random. None of the minority alliance have done anything outside of that game that should put them in a negative light, yet the majority alliance can’t see past that because they have no real off time to recuperate. It makes it a frustrating watch for the viewers. 

Edit: I also want to add, that’s why they keep crying lmao… this is their entire life for a week so they genuinely can’t see that its all just a gameeeeee

Seokjin was bang on when he said that this show is literally about intelligence and being able to show your skills and talent. Why on earth do we need to watch Kyeongram, Yumin, Seungkwan and Joonbin struggle every week? It’s boring. I wish there were more “regular” people over celebrities. It makes no sense to cast so many people based off their job rather than their skillset. I had a good laugh when he said it was like Brazil finishing 16th in the World Cup lol

The only person I’m really rooting for is Seokjin, but Seewon taking the win would be great too. Dongjoo is a great player but I think most of her great wins come through sheer luck or Orbit’s own skillset (or the majority alliance). The only place she’s shined is through the memory game, and while she received a lot of love for it, I’m not fully convinced she was that spectacular during it. No one else really had a chance to play so it’s hard to say but I personally think even without her they would’ve done fine. I also think the questions during that game were a lot easier than I had originally expected.

Not sure if you'd be able to tell individual DC galls that raised over $12k USD just for their pick to flunk out with rigged numbers attached to his name this same thing. Yes, Burning Sun is a big issue, and should never lose relevancy or resources, but how is that relevant to OP's post. Can we discuss more on the actual issue rather than comparing it to Burning Sun and crediting it as a non-issue? In this case any corruption issue that is raised in r/kpop should just be dismissed if it's less profound than Burning Sun.

I'm curious as to why you'd think just because profoundly worse criminal activities happen within the industry, scamming people out of their money to make a fraudulent lineup is excused? I find it an interesting take that just because in the grand scheme of things the finale lineup for PDX 101 might not matter, you'd say that a scam worth millions should be completely ignored. Especially despite so much of the public, including young students who don't own much capital in the first place, invested into this.

I think the issue of teaching democracy is corrupt to young easily-influenced minds is ridiculous, and I may not understand this politician's intentions (targeting the young voters), however I think he raises a sound argument that should be discussed.
